originality.rationale: The exact odd-order centered-polygonal symmetry locus and the quintic Frobenius formula were compared at the implication/domain level with classical gluing (Fel 2008), ordinary triangular/tetrahedral tuples (Robles-Pérez/Rosales 2017), and generalized star triples (Yin/Mu/Komatsu 2024). The latter requires integer coefficient a>=4 and hence even centered polygon order 2a, while the present claim requires odd order k>=3. Published articles and the OEIS sequence entry were compared for aliases, parameter ranges, and stronger implication statements. No covering claim was found; the possibility of unlocated equivalence remains.
residual_risks: The complete 2024 generalized-star-number article could not be inspected; its explicit integer-parameter/even-order scope excludes direct coverage, but indirect external equivalence is not ruled out.
Unindexed or inaccessible publications may contain an equivalent special case or elementary gluing reformulation; absence of retrieved matches is not mathematical proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Natural two-parameter centered odd polygonal family has precisely one symmetric semigroup in each polygon order after the geometrically meaningful stable layer n>=k; explicit quintic Frobenius and genus supplied. The low-index restriction is essential, not an arbitrary computational slice. This completes a symmetry classification absent from checked even-centered and ordinary figurate work; neither correctness nor computational reproducibility is used alone as a value argument.
